e: Construction begins on the high-speed rail line between Porto and Lisbon.
Protests held in several cities across the country against the rising cost of living and housing.
Protests against rising fuel prices lead hundreds of truck drivers to hold a slow march along several roads nationwide.
Public Prosecution conducts searches at the facilities of the Judiciary Police due to suspicions of the use of illegal wiretaps in the Football Leaks case.
The Assembly of the Republic rejects the motion of no confidence against the government.
Opposition leader André Ventura submits a motion of no confidence against the government in light of the controversies surrounding minister of home affairs Luís Neves.
President António José Seguro approves the new "Law of Return," following an unanimous vote by the Constitutional Court in favor of the changes.
Twelve people are injured, some seriously, after a drunken hit-and-run in Albufeira.
Two soldiers are killed after being hit by a car on the A1 motorway in Mealhada, while assisting a stopped truck driver.
President Seguro promulgates the so-called "burqa law", which outlaws face concealment in public spaces.
Several wildfires break out, causing injuries, some critical, to firefighters.
British cyclist Finlay Tarling is killed in a collision with a light goods vehicle with during the eighth stage of the 2026 Volta a Portugal.

A total solar eclipse occurs at the Moon's descending node of the orbit in North America and Europe. The total eclipse passes over the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean, northeastern Portugal and northern Spain.
A Swedish tourist is hit by a stray bullet during a fight related to drug dealing in Lisbon Baixa.
Two earthquakes, with magnitude of 3.3, are felt in Lisbon district and the Alentejo region. No damage or victims are reported.

President António José Seguro sends the proposed changes to the "Law of Return" to the Constitutional Court, raising concerns about the possibility of separating parents from children or expelling minor Portuguese naturalized children.
A bus crashes into the façade of Tomar's hospital, killing one person and seriously injuring three others.

Public Prosecution opens an inquiry into the management of Luís Neves, current minister of home affairs, in his former role as director of the Judiciary Police, in relation to alleged crimes of smuggling and abuse of power in a case concerning the loan of a seized drug trailer to a contractor friend of his.
Grades for the Secondary Education National Exams begin to be published following several problems with the new digital classification process, which created delays and errors.
Almada declares a state of alert because of a water supply crisis, due to low reservoirs, leading to cuts and rationing for the population.
A bus accident at Agualva-Cacém railway station leaves two dead and 20 injured.
The government activates the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM) because of wildfires and a heat wave which dangerously increases the risk of further wildfires.
A 4.1 magnitude earthquake is felt in the Algarve. No damage or victims are reported.
The Assembly of the Republic rejects the government's labour reform, with far-right Chega and center-left to left-wing parties blocking the proposed legislation.
Public Prosecution charges members of the neo-Nazi Movimento Armilar Lusitano of planning attacks against Luís Montenegro, António Costa, former living Presidents, and other well-known personalities.
Killing of Odair Moniz: A Sintra court judge sentences the police officer who shot Odair Moniz in October 2024 to three and a half years of suspended imprisonment.
President António José Seguro vetoes a parliamentary bill that would ban "ideological flags" from being displayed on public buildings.
A general strike, the second in six months, is called by the General Confederation of the Portuguese Workers (CGTP) against the government's labour reforms.
Portugal is elected to a rotating seat at the United Nations Security Council.
A French couple, mother and stepfather, are arrested by Portuguese police after abandoning their children, two boys both under the age of 5, on a road near Alcácer do Sal, in Setúbal district.
The Constitutional Court strikes down the nationality law decree that would allow the criminal penalty of loss of citizenship for immigrants who commit serious crimes.
A soldier undertaking a parachuting course dies after an accident at Tancos air base.
Negotiations between employers' associations, unions, and the government regarding the new labour legislation end without an agreement.
Fifteen police officers are detained following an investigation on cases of alleged torture of migrants and homeless at two central Lisbon precincts.
President António José Seguro promulgates the recent changes to the nationality law.
The Judiciary Police arrest a man who tried to sell 278 paintings, some possibly by Pablo Picasso and Joan Miró, illegally in the black market.

The Socialist Party (PS) asks the Constitutional Court to rule on a decree of the new nationality law regarding the penalty of loss of nationality for immigrants who have acquired citizenship and then commit serious crimes.
The Portuguese government requests support from the European Union Solidarity Fund due to the winter storms.
The 1976 Constitution marks 50 years since its approval.
A new nationality law is approved by the Assembly of the Republic, in response to several parts of the previous proposal that were rejected by the Constitutional Court in November 2025.
